Launch the dppca Shiny app

Source: R/dppca_app.R
dppca_app.Rd

Launches an interactive 'shiny' application for exploring differentially private PCA visualizations. The PCA tab uses dp_pca() for integrated estimation, summaries, and scree, score, loading, variable, and biplot displays, including grouped score plots when grouping is enabled. The Loading, Scree, and Score tabs provide standalone analyses, including method comparisons and grouped score plots.

Usage

dppca_app(X = NULL, group = NULL)

Arguments

X

A numeric matrix or data frame with observations in rows and variables in columns. Non-numeric data-frame columns are excluded with a warning; numeric values must be finite. Input is not automatically centered or standardized. If provided, the app uses this dataset initially. At least two observations and two numeric features are required.

group

Optional group column name in X or vector of group labels (NULL by default). A selected group column is excluded from PCA features, even when numeric; group labels and membership are assumed public. Only used with supplied X; activate grouping in the PCA or Score tab to use these labels.

Value

Invisibly returns the value produced by shiny::runApp() after the application exits.

Details

The app accepts built-in data, supplied X, or uploaded CSV files. Grouping is available for PCA and Score analyses; a selected group column is excluded from numeric PCA features. Loading and Scree analyses use all numeric feature columns.

Running an analysis stores its estimates for subsequent plotting. Display settings can redraw an existing fit without consuming another privacy budget. Non-private reference output is optional in the app and is not a private release. Budget tables display allocations but do not track cumulative privacy cost across runs.

Input is not automatically centered or standardized. Any data-dependent preprocessing requires separate privacy accounting; see dp_pca() and dp_score() for applicable conditions.

Examples

if (interactive()) {
# Launch the app with built-in example datasets.
dppca_app()

# Launch the app with a user-supplied numeric dataset.
data(gau, package = "dppca")
dppca_app(gau)

# Launch the app with group labels stored in a column.
data(gau_g, package = "dppca")
dppca_app(gau_g, group = "group")
}
